query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a ceramic or refractory metal coating to the surface of boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment will improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment
generation.intervention: Applying a ceramic or refractory metal coating to the surface
generation.mechanism: Formation of a protective layer that prevents direct contact with molten aluminum
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion by 30% compared to uncoated components
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in corrosion resistance may vary depending on the specific coating material and application method

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with coated and uncoated boride-based components exposed to molten aluminum under identical operating conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate of the coated components is not at least 20% lower than that of the uncoated components, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: It was found that, by reducing the Mn concentration (to 5 at.% Mn), the CoCrFeMnNi alloy acquires higher yield strength values after annealing at 1117 K (from 387 to 477 MPa) due to the grain refinement effect (from 4.4 to 2.61 µm) []. Mn also shows a rapid evaporation effect during melting processes; hence, in our study, this element was replaced by Mo, which could improve the resistance to high temperatures []. Co–Cr–Mo alloy is widely used for manufacturing of vanes and gas turbines due to its excellent fatigue behavior and wear resistance [,,,]. In such alloys, molybdenum has a beneficial effect on passivation capacity, contributing to the formation of a protective surface layer that allows pitting corrosion to be limited [,]. Studies were conducted to estimate the effects on the microstructure and properties of alloys with different Mo contents [,,]. Such alloys have been designed for the manufacture of furnace casings and chemical tanks used in high-temperature and corrosion conditions [], for components used in the geothermal industry [,], or to obtain high-performance coatings [].

In this study, a reinforced layer was prepared on the surface of HEA by powder-pack boriding and focused on the effect of temperature and duration on the boronizing of CoCrFeNiMn HEA. The boronized samples were characterized using various methods. Furthermore, the properties of boronized CoCrFeNiMn alloys and diffusion behavior were investigated. This study could provide a reference for high hardness and high wear resistance HEA that could be used in a variety of industrial applications, such as the mold and crucible used in the cast aluminum industry [,], because the borides formed on the surface have high hardness, excellent corrosion resistance, and wear resistance [,], which allow HEA to be applied in special environments to increase service life.

In addition, to obtain a uniform and stable protective layer, sputtering technology offers a fast deposition rate and a low-cost solution. Although the development of HEA systems has been going on for more than a decade, there are few reports on the deposition of stable protective films on HEA surfaces by conventional reactive sputtering techniques. Many studies have shown that sputter deposition of CrN film on conventional stainless steel is beneficial for its wear and corrosion resistance [,]. The CrN film deposited on the surface of 316 stainless steel has a positive effect on the friction behavior in NaCl solution and high temperature environments until heated to 550 °C []. In the tribo-corrosion test, the CrN coating layer can also remain relatively stable during the ball-on-plate sliding under various applied potentials []. As stainless steels are similar to CoCrNi-based MEAs in terms of their single FCC structure and lattice constant, this study attempts to sputter CrN film with a Cr buffer layer on the surface of CoCrNiSi0.3 MEA and discusses in detail the improvement of corrosion and wear resistance of CoCrNiSi0.3 MEA by sputtering CrN film.
